clue.text: Singer charged nothing following pay-off

indicators.note: following tells us the pay-off piece is followed by the rest

parts.note: a sop is a bribe or pay-off given to placate someone
to charge is to rush or run, so charged gives ran
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A vocalist was billed nothing after receiving a settlement payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts SOP first; the order is pay-off, then charged, then nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest female or boy's voice.

clue.text: Dog needing publicity entered in Cruft's, perhaps

indicators.note: entered in says publicity goes inside the show

parts.note: Crufts is a famous British dog show, an example of a show
an ad is publicity

explanation.surface: A dog needs publicity to be entered at a top dog show.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's best-known dog show; 'Dog' as a verb means to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, as a shadow does.

clue.text: Lively drama all but sold out?

parts.note: a play is a drama

indicators.note: all but means the word except its final letter

parts.note: a show that has sold out is full

explanation.surface: A lively play that has almost sold out its seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' trims FULL to FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful and lively both describe high-spirited, frisky behaviour; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Off around the globe, taking it all in

indicators.note: around says absent goes round the next piece

parts.note: off can mean away or not present, absent
an orb is a globe or sphere

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off round the world, soaking up everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' is in the sense of being off work, absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absorbent soaks liquid up, taking it all in.

clue.text: Island visited regularly for an hour

indicators.note: visited regularly means calling at every other letter, here the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th

explanation.surface: An island that is called at on a regular schedule for an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of fOr An HoUr give the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Oahu is the Hawaiian island where Honolulu stands.

clue.text: Direct, with overlap

indicators.note: overlap says the two pieces share their touching letter, so one copy of the shared A goes

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed in the clue is itself named: a comma
with can mean and, as in 'bread with butter'

explanation.surface: A terse instruction to send something straight on, complete with an overlap.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed comma is part of the wordplay: COMMA and AND overlap on their shared A, giving COMMAND.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct people is to give them orders, to command them; a synonym as verbs.

clue.text: Become engaged, finding: girl superficially attractive

parts.note: a mechanism that catches becomes engaged, like a latch
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man gets engaged after meeting a girl who is only skin-deep attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become engaged' suggests marriage but means to catch, as gears do; 'finding' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchpenny describes goods that are cheap and showy, designed only to attract sales.

clue.text: Court official, male, runs to embrace champion

indicators.note: to embrace means the male and runs pieces enclose the champion

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: A male court official runs to hug the champion.
explanation.walkthrough: M and R sit either side of ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A macer is an official who carries the mace in a Scottish court of law.

clue.text: Bishop appeared to be under a doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming after

parts.note: MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor
rose can mean appeared, as the moon rose

explanation.surface: A bishop seems to be placed under the care of a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to be under' means coming after the other pieces; MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the usual crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ambrose was the fourth-century Bishop of Milan.

clue.text: Blindingly impressive?

parts.note: the phrase reads as very striking, and literally as so bright it stops you seeing

explanation.definitionFit: Light so bright it blinds is dazzling, and so is a stunning performance.

clue.text: One artistic code of a number used in theatre

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
an aesthetic is a set of principles guiding an artist, an artistic code

explanation.surface: A performer's single artistic principle concerns a song number staged at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a song but something that numbs, and the theatre is an operating theatre; 'of a' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that numbs a patient during surgery in an operating theatre is an anaesthetic.

clue.text: Sketch writer's book having little weight

parts.note: oz, the ounce, is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: An author of sketches has a slim, lightweight volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens published 'Sketches by Boz' under this pen name; 'having' is link and the possessive in the definition reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boz was the pen name Dickens used for his early collection of sketches.

clue.text: Body heartily 'carries vote in favour of University

indicators.note: carries means the heart of body holds the next pieces within it
heartily asks for the heart of the word body, its two middle letters

parts.note: X is the cross marked on a ballot paper as a vote
for means in favour of, as in 'for the motion'

explanation.surface: A student body enthusiastically passes a motion backing its university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily' asks for the two middle letters of 'Body', and 'carries' places the vote and 'in favour of' within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is the name of the ancient English university, an example of the category.

clue.text: Check curve round a lake, using coloured sticks

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
an arc is a curve
O is round in shape
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An artist checks a curve around a lake, drawing with coloured sticks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcoal comes as dark sticks of carbon that artists draw with.

clue.text: Sorry-looking forgery vandalised once penny first drops

parts.note: a sham is a fake or forgery

indicators.note: first drops says the penny letter at the start is removed

parts.note: vandalised means defaced
D was the symbol for a penny in old British money

explanation.surface: A guilty-looking forger vandalises the work until the penny drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once penny' is pre-decimal British money, whose pence were written d; 'first drops' takes the D off DEFACED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shamefaced looks ashamed, sorry for what they did.

clue.text: Land Chinese title after hammering Nanking's No 1

indicators.note: hammering means beating into a new shape, so the words before are rearranged

parts.note: the number one, first letter of Nanking is N

explanation.surface: A country takes a Chinese title after beating the leader of Nanking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after hammering' signals the anagram of the first two words; the scan prints 'No 1', meaning the leading letter of Nanking.
explanation.definitionFit: Liechtenstein is a small Alpine principality, an example of a land or country.

clue.text: Arnold's second chapter on British needs measure of work

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Arnold's second chapter about Britain requires a measure of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Arnold's' reads as 'Arnold is'; 'needs' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Schoenberg was the Austrian composer; here the surname is written without the e.

clue.text: Exchange rate only found in N. Italy?

indicators.note: to exchange is to swap round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: This exchange rate is said to be used only in northern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The South Tyrol is in northern Italy, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrolean means from the Tyrol, an Alpine region partly in northern Italy.

clue.text: Moving skilfully to trade blows perhaps, smash tiny chap to pulp

definitions.text: Moving skilfully to trade blows perhaps

indicators.note: reducing something to pulp destroys its shape, so the letters are mashed up

explanation.surface: A fighter moves deftly to exchange punches and beat a small man to pulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trade blows' suggests boxing, but the trade winds blow; sailing with them skilfully is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in handling a sailing boat with the trade winds is seamanship of the yacht kind.

clue.text: Sandstone houses new — no old dwelling

indicators.note: houses means the sandstone holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: crag is a geological name for a shelly sandstone, and a rock outcrop

explanation.surface: Sandstone homes are new, not ancient dwellings.
explanation.walkthrough: Crag is a geologist's word for a shelly sandstone in East Anglia; the dash is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A crannog is an ancient lake dwelling built on an artificial island in Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Forced to serve crushed juice

definitions.meaning: men ... into the navy were forced into service by press gangs
fruit juice squeezed out by crushing is described as ...

explanation.walkthrough: Press gangs forced men to serve in the British navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pressed means being compelled, and fruit squeezed hard is likewise pressed for its juice.

clue.text: Sally meeting zany guy on vacation, forming couple

indicators.note: vacated words are emptied, keeping only first and last letters

explanation.surface: Sally meets a zany guy while on holiday, and they become a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' and 'forming' are link words; each word's first and last letters give SY, ZY, GY.
explanation.definitionFit: Syzygy means a pair or conjunction, especially of heavenly bodies in alignment.

clue.text: Switch can never be this spasmodic

definitions.meaning: a switch is in one state or the other, never both positions at once
spasmodic means intermittent, happening in fits and starts

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the phrase literally: a switch cannot be both at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intermittent stops and starts, coming and going in fits.

clue.text: Resign from duty initially before' period is up

indicators.note: before says the duty letter comes first
initially means the first letter of duty
in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a period is a time

explanation.surface: Someone resigns from duty before the period is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' turns TIME into EMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To demit is to resign or give up an office, chiefly Scottish usage.

clue.text: Completely gutted, girl left French town

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A girl left a French town utterly devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely gutted' leaves CY; 'left' is a link word here, not the abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: Annecy is a lakeside town in the Haute-Savoie region of France.

clue.text: Graze bullocks, keep ox penned

indicators.note: penned means held within, so the answer is hidden inside the words

explanation.surface: Farm advice: graze the bullocks, and keep the ox in a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across graZE BUllocks; 'keep' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The zebu is a humped domestic ox of India.

clue.text: Trotsky missed out on Liberal period

indicators.note: missed out on means the named letter is left out of the name

parts.note: Leon Trotsky was the Russian revolutionary

explanation.surface: The revolutionary failed to join the Liberals for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: Trotsky's first name LEON loses the L for Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is a very long stretch of time, an age.

clue.text: Clerk makes blunders with ultimately tricky high-level pattern

indicators.note: blunders suggests a muddle, so the letters of the preceding words are jumbled
ultimately points to the final letter of tricky

explanation.surface: An office clerk keeps making mistakes with a tricky elevated design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the Y from tricky to the anagram of CLERK MAKES.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky streaked with rippled cirrocumulus cloud, like fish scales, forms a pattern high up.

clue.text: Denied new drug restricted movement of pupils

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a gated schoolchild is confined to school grounds as punishment

explanation.surface: A school denies giving a new drug and confined its pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gated' is a British school punishment: pupils kept within the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate something is to deny or contradict it, so negated is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Defying belief, being so early?

definitions.meaning: defying belief here means irreligious, rejecting faith in God
an outrageously early hour is called by this name in idiom

explanation.walkthrough: 'Defying belief' looks like 'incredible' but means without religion.
explanation.definitionFit: An unreasonably early time is idiomatically an hour no decent person would keep; irreligious people are wicked.
